that the bytes contain valid WTF-8.

For the safe version, see [Wtf8Buf::from_bytes](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/ecma/atoms/hstr/wtf8/struct.Wtf8Buf.html#method.from_bytes).

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#safety)Safety

The bytes passed in must be valid WTF-8. See [Wtf8Buf::from_bytes](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/ecma/atoms/hstr/wtf8/struct.Wtf8Buf.html#method.from_bytes) for
the requirements.

Return the length, in WTF-8 bytes.

Return `true` if the string has a length of zero bytes.

Return `true` if the string contains only ASCII characters.

`__ecma` and `ecma_ast`Convert the WTF-8 string to potentially ill-formed UTF-16 and return an iterator of 16-bit code units.

This is lossless:
calling `Wtf8Buf::from_ill_formed_utf16` on the resulting code units
would always return the original WTF-8 string.

Remove duplicates from sections of consecutive identical elements, while keeping a count of
how many repeated elements were present.
This will determine equality using a comparison function.
If the iterator is sorted, all elements will be unique.

[Read more]If there are elements and they are all equal, return a single copy of that element.
If there are no elements, return an Error containing None.
If there are elements and they are not all equal, return a tuple containing the first
two non-equal elements found.

the cell was empty. If the cell was empty and `f` failed, an
error is returned.

If several threads concurrently run `get_or_init`, more than one `f` can
be called. However, all threads will return the same value, produced by
some `f`.

# Lazy in swc_core::base::atoms::once_cell::sync - Rust

# Struct Lazy

`pub struct Lazy<T, F = `[fn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.fn.html)() -> T> { /* private fields */ }**crate feature**only.

`__base`## Expand description

A value which is initialized on the first access.

This type is thread-safe and can be used in statics.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example)Example

```
use std::collections::HashMap;
use once_cell::sync::Lazy;
static HASHMAP: Lazy<HashMap<i32, String>> = Lazy::new(|| {
    println!("initializing");
    let mut m = HashMap::new();
    m.insert(13, "Spica".to_string());
    m.insert(74, "Hoyten".to_string());
    m
});
fn main() {
    println!("ready");
    std::thread::spawn(|| {
        println!("{:?}", HASHMAP.get(&13));
    }).join().unwrap();
    println!("{:?}", HASHMAP.get(&74));
    // Prints:
    //   ready
    //   initializing
    //   Some("Spica")
    //   Some("Hoyten")
}
```
## Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#implementations)

# OnceCell in swc_core::base::atoms::once_cell::sync - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_core/base/atoms/once_cell/sync/struct.OnceCell.html

# Struct OnceCell

`pub struct OnceCell<T>(/* private fields */);`**crate feature**only.

`__base`## Expand description

A thread-safe cell which can be written to only once.

`OnceCell` provides `&` references to the contents without RAII guards.

Reading a non-`None` value out of `OnceCell` establishes a
happens-before relationship with a corresponding write. For example, if
thread A initializes the cell with `get_or_init(f)`, and thread B
subsequently reads the result of this call, B also observes all the side
effects of `f`.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example)Example

```
use once_cell::sync::OnceCell;
static CELL: OnceCell<String> = OnceCell::new();
assert!(CELL.get().is_none());
std::thread::spawn(|| {
    let value: &String = CELL.get_or_init(|| {
        "Hello, World!".to_string()
    });
    assert_eq!(value, "Hello, World!");
}).join().unwrap();
let value: Option<&String> = CELL.get();
assert!(value.is_some());
assert_eq!(value.unwrap().as_str(), "Hello, World!");
```
## Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#implementations)

Creates a new empty cell.

#### pub const fn [with_value](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.with_value)(value: T) -> [OnceCell](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/common/sync/struct.OnceCell.html)<T>

**crate features **`__ecma` and `ecma_ast` only.

#### pub const fn [with_value](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.with_value)(value: T) -> [OnceCell](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/common/sync/struct.OnceCell.html)<T>

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `ecma_ast`Creates a new initialized cell.

Gets the reference to the underlying value.

Returns `None` if the cell is empty, or being initialized. This
method never blocks.

Gets the reference to the underlying value, blocking the current thread until it is set.

```
use once_cell::sync::OnceCell;
let mut cell = std::sync::Arc::new(OnceCell::new());
let t = std::thread::spawn({
    let cell = std::sync::Arc::clone(&cell);
    move || cell.set(92).unwrap()
});
// Returns immediately, but might return None.
let _value_or_none = cell.get();
// Will return 92, but might block until the other thread does `.set`.
let value: &u32 = cell.wait();
assert_eq!(*value, 92);
t.join().unwrap();
```
Gets the mutable reference to the underlying value.

Returns `None` if the cell is empty.

This method is allowed to violate the invariant of writing to a `OnceCell`
at most once because it requires `&mut` access to `self`. As with all
interior mutability, `&mut` access permits arbitrary modification:

```
use once_cell::sync::OnceCell;
let mut cell: OnceCell<u32> = OnceCell::new();
cell.set(92).unwrap();
cell = OnceCell::new();
```
#### pub unsafe fn [get_unchecked](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_unchecked)(&self) -> [&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

**crate features **`__ecma` and `ecma_ast` only.

#### pub unsafe fn [get_unchecked](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_unchecked)(&self) -> [&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `ecma_ast`Get the reference to the underlying value, without checking if the cell is initialized.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#safety)Safety

Caller must ensure that the cell is in initialized state, and that the contents are acquired by (synchronized to) this thread.

Sets the contents of this cell to `value`.

Returns `Ok(())` if the cell was empty and `Err(value)` if it was
full.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example-1)Example

```
use once_cell::sync::OnceCell;
static CELL: OnceCell<i32> = OnceCell::new();
fn main() {
    assert!(CELL.get().is_none());
    std::thread::spawn(|| {
        assert_eq!(CELL.set(92), Ok(()));
    }).join().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(CELL.set(62), Err(62));
    assert_eq!(CELL.get(), Some(&92));
}
```

**crate features **`__ecma` and `ecma_ast` only.

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `ecma_ast`#### pub fn [get_or_init](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_or_init)<F>(&self, f: F) -> [&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

**crate features **`__ecma` and `ecma_ast` only.

#### pub fn [get_or_init](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_or_init)<F>(&self, f: F) -> [&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `ecma_ast`Gets the contents of the cell, initializing it with `f` if the cell
was empty.

Many threads may call `get_or_init` concurrently with different
initializing functions, but it is guaranteed that only one function
will be executed.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics)Panics

If `f` panics, the panic is propagated to the caller, and the cell
remains uninitialized.

It is an error to reentrantly initialize the cell from `f`. The
exact outcome is unspecified. Current implementation deadlocks, but
this may be changed to a panic in the future.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example-3)Example

```
use once_cell::sync::OnceCell;
let cell = OnceCell::new();
let value = cell.get_or_init(|| 92);
assert_eq!(value, &92);
let value = cell.get_or_init(|| unreachable!());
assert_eq!(value, &92);
```

**crate features **`__ecma` and `ecma_ast` only.

#### pub fn [get_or_try_init](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_or_try_init)<F, E>(&self, f: F) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html), E>

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `ecma_ast`Gets the contents of the cell, initializing it with `f` if
the cell was empty. If the cell was empty and `f` failed, an
error is returned.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics-1)Panics

If `f` panics, the panic is propagated to the caller, and
the cell remains uninitialized.

It is an error to reentrantly initialize the cell from `f`.
The exact outcome is unspecified. Current implementation
deadlocks, but this may be changed to a panic in the future.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example-4)Example

```
use once_cell::sync::OnceCell;
let cell = OnceCell::new();
assert_eq!(cell.get_or_try_init(|| Err(())), Err(()));
assert!(cell.get().is_none());
let value = cell.get_or_try_init(|| -> Result<i32, ()> {
    Ok(92)
});
assert_eq!(value, Ok(&92));
assert_eq!(cell.get(), Some(&92))
```
Takes the value out of this `OnceCell`, moving it back to an uninitialized state.

Has no effect and returns `None` if the `OnceCell` hasn’t been initialized.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples)Examples

```
use once_cell::sync::OnceCell;
let mut cell: OnceCell<String> = OnceCell::new();
assert_eq!(cell.take(), None);
let mut cell = OnceCell::new();
cell.set("hello".to_string()).unwrap();
assert_eq!(cell.take(), Some("hello".to_string()));
assert_eq!(cell.get(), None);
```
This method is allowed to violate the invariant of writing to a `OnceCell`
at most once because it requires `&mut` access to `self`. As with all
interior mutability, `&mut` access permits arbitrary modification:

```
use once_cell::sync::OnceCell;
let mut cell: OnceCell<u32> = OnceCell::new();
cell.set(92).unwrap();
cell = OnceCell::new();
```

A value which is initialized on the first access.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example)Example

```

    println!("initializing");
    92
});

// Prints:
//   ready
//   initializing
//   92
//   92
```

# OnceCell in swc_core::base::atoms::once_cell::unsync - Rust

# Struct OnceCell

`pub struct OnceCell<T> { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`__base`## Expand description

A cell which can be written to only once. It is not thread safe.

Unlike [ std::cell::RefCell](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/cell/struct.RefCell.html), a

`OnceCell` provides simple `&`
references to the contents.[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example)Example

```
use once_cell::unsync::OnceCell;
let cell = OnceCell::new();
assert!(cell.get().is_none());
let value: &String = cell.get_or_init(|| {
    "Hello, World!".to_string()
});
assert_eq!(value, "Hello, World!");
assert!(cell.get().is_some());
```
## Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#implementations)

Creates a new empty cell.

#### pub const fn [with_value](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.with_value)(value: T) -> [OnceCell](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/ecma/atoms/once_cell/unsync/struct.OnceCell.html)<T>

**crate features **`__ecma` and `ecma_ast` only.

#### pub const fn [with_value](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.with_value)(value: T) -> [OnceCell](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/ecma/atoms/once_cell/unsync/struct.OnceCell.html)<T>

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `ecma_ast`Creates a new initialized cell.

Gets a reference to the underlying value.

Returns `None` if the cell is empty.

Gets a mutable reference to the underlying value.

Returns `None` if the cell is empty.

This method is allowed to violate the invariant of writing to a `OnceCell`
at most once because it requires `&mut` access to `self`. As with all
interior mutability, `&mut` access permits arbitrary modification:

```
use once_cell::unsync::OnceCell;
let mut cell: OnceCell<u32> = OnceCell::new();
cell.set(92).unwrap();
*cell.get_mut().unwrap() = 93;
assert_eq!(cell.get(), Some(&93));
```
Sets the contents of this cell to `value`.

Returns `Ok(())` if the cell was empty and `Err(value)` if it was
full.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example-1)Example

```
use once_cell::unsync::OnceCell;
let cell = OnceCell::new();
assert!(cell.get().is_none());
assert_eq!(cell.set(92), Ok(()));
assert_eq!(cell.set(62), Err(62));
assert!(cell.get().is_some());
```

#### pub fn [get_or_init](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_or_init)<F>(&self, f: F) -> [&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `ecma_ast`Gets the contents of the cell, initializing it with `f`
if the cell was empty.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics)Panics

If `f` panics, the panic is propagated to the caller, and the cell
remains uninitialized.

It is an error to reentrantly initialize the cell from `f`. Doing
so results in a panic.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example-3)Example

```
use once_cell::unsync::OnceCell;
let cell = OnceCell::new();
let value = cell.get_or_init(|| 92);
assert_eq!(value, &92);
let value = cell.get_or_init(|| unreachable!());
assert_eq!(value, &92);
```

#### pub fn [get_or_try_init](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_or_try_init)<F, E>(&self, f: F) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html), E>

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `ecma_ast`Gets the contents of the cell, initializing it with `f` if
the cell was empty. If the cell was empty and `f` failed, an
error is returned.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics-1)Panics

If `f` panics, the panic is propagated to the caller, and the cell
remains uninitialized.

It is an error to reentrantly initialize the cell from `f`. Doing
so results in a panic.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example-4)Example

```
use once_cell::unsync::OnceCell;
let cell = OnceCell::new();
assert_eq!(cell.get_or_try_init(|| Err(())), Err(()));
assert!(cell.get().is_none());
let value = cell.get_or_try_init(|| -> Result<i32, ()> {
    Ok(92)
});
assert_eq!(value, Ok(&92));
assert_eq!(cell.get(), Some(&92))
```
Takes the value out of this `OnceCell`, moving it back to an uninitialized state.

Has no effect and returns `None` if the `OnceCell` hasn’t been initialized.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples)Examples

```
use once_cell::unsync::OnceCell;
let mut cell: OnceCell<String> = OnceCell::new();
assert_eq!(cell.take(), None);
let mut cell = OnceCell::new();
cell.set("hello".to_string()).unwrap();
assert_eq!(cell.take(), Some("hello".to_string()));
assert_eq!(cell.get(), None);
```
This method is allowed to violate the invariant of writing to a `OnceCell`
at most once because it requires `&mut` access to `self`. As with all
interior mutability, `&mut` access permits arbitrary modification:

```
use once_cell::unsync::OnceCell;
let mut cell: OnceCell<u32> = OnceCell::new();
cell.set(92).unwrap();
cell = OnceCell::new();
```

# PluginConfig in swc_core::base::config - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_core/base/config/struct.PluginConfig.html

**crate feature**only.

`__base`## Expand description

A tuple represents a plugin.

First element is a resolvable name to the plugin, second is a JSON object that represents configuration option for those plugin. Type of plugin’s configuration is up to each plugin - swc/core does not have strong type and it’ll be serialized into plain string when it’s passed to plugin’s entrypoint function.

Remove duplicates from sections of consecutive identical elements, while keeping a count of
how many repeated elements were present.
This will determine equality using a comparison function.
If the iterator is sorted, all elements will be unique.

[Read more]If there are elements and they are all equal, return a single copy of that element.
If there are no elements, return an Error containing None.
If there are elements and they are not all equal, return a tuple containing the first
two non-equal elements found.

`__base`## Expand description

Represents a raw token

Raw tokens are used internally to represent the sourcemap in a memory efficient way. If you construct sourcemaps yourself then you need to create these objects, otherwise they are invisible to you as a user.

`__base`## Expand description

Controls the `SourceMap::rewrite` behavior

Default configuration:

- `with_names`: true
- `with_source_contents`: true
- `load_local_source_contents`: false

## Fields[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#fields)

Remove duplicates from sections of consecutive identical elements, while keeping a count of
how many repeated elements were present.
This will determine equality using a comparison function.
If the iterator is sorted, all elements will be unique.

[Read more]If there are elements and they are all equal, return a single copy of that element.
If there are no elements, return an Error containing None.
If there are elements and they are not all equal, return a tuple containing the first
two non-equal elements found.

Remove duplicates from sections of consecutive identical elements, while keeping a count of
how many repeated elements were present.
This will determine equality using a comparison function.
If the iterator is sorted, all elements will be unique.

[Read more]If there are elements and they are all equal, return a single copy of that element.
If there are no elements, return an Error containing None.
If there are elements and they are not all equal, return a tuple containing the first
two non-equal elements found.

# SourceMap in swc_core::base::sourcemap - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_core/base/sourcemap/struct.SourceMap.html

# Struct SourceMap

`pub struct SourceMap { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`__base`## Expand description

Represents a sourcemap in memory

This is always represents a regular “non-indexed” sourcemap.  Particularly
in case the `from_reader` method is used an index sourcemap will be
rejected with an error on reading.

## Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#implementations)

#### pub fn [from_reader](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.from_reader)<R>(rdr: R) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html), [Error](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Error.html)>

#### pub fn [from_reader](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.from_reader)<R>(rdr: R) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html), [Error](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Error.html)>

Creates a sourcemap from a reader over a JSON stream in UTF-8 format. Optionally a “garbage header” as defined by the sourcemap draft specification is supported. In case an indexed sourcemap is encountered an error is returned.

```
use swc_sourcemap::SourceMap;
let input: &[_] = b"{
    \"version\":3,
    \"sources\":[\"coolstuff.js\"],
    \"names\":[\"x\",\"alert\"],
    \"mappings\":\"AAAA,GAAIA,GAAI,EACR,IAAIA,GAAK,EAAG,CACVC,MAAM\"
}";
let sm = SourceMap::from_reader(input).unwrap();
```
While sourcemaps objects permit some modifications, it’s generally
not possible to modify tokens after they have been added.  For
creating sourcemaps from scratch or for general operations for
modifying a sourcemap have a look at the `SourceMapBuilder`.

Writes a sourcemap into a writer.

Note that this operation will generate an equivalent sourcemap to the
one that was generated on load however there might be small differences
in the generated JSON and layout. For instance `sourceRoot` will not
be set as upon parsing of the sourcemap the sources will already be
expanded.

```
let sm = SourceMap::from_reader(input).unwrap();
let mut output : Vec<u8> = vec![];
sm.to_writer(&mut output).unwrap();
```

#### pub fn [to_data_url](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.to_data_url)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [Error](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Error.html)>

#### pub fn [from_slice](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.from_slice)(slice: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)]) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html), [Error](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Error.html)>

#### pub fn [from_slice](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.from_slice)(slice: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)]) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html), [Error](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Error.html)>

Creates a sourcemap from a reader over a JSON byte slice in UTF-8 format. Optionally a “garbage header” as defined by the sourcemap draft specification is supported. In case an indexed sourcemap is encountered an error is returned.

```
use swc_sourcemap::SourceMap;
let input: &[_] = b"{
    \"version\":3,
    \"sources\":[\"coolstuff.js\"],
    \"names\":[\"x\",\"alert\"],
    \"mappings\":\"AAAA,GAAIA,GAAI,EACR,IAAIA,GAAK,EAAG,CACVC,MAAM\"
}";
let sm = SourceMap::from_slice(input).unwrap();
```
Constructs a new sourcemap from raw components.

- `file`: an optional filename of the sourcemap
- `tokens`: a list of raw tokens
- `names`: a vector of names
- `sources`a vector of source filenames
- `sources_content`optional source contents
- `ignore_list`optional list of source indexes for devtools to ignore

#### pub fn [rewrite](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.rewrite)(self, options: &[RewriteOptions](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.RewriteOptions.html)<'_>) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html), [Error](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Error.html)>

#### pub fn [rewrite](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.rewrite)(self, options: &[RewriteOptions](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.RewriteOptions.html)<'_>) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html), [Error](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Error.html)>

This rewrites the sourcemap according to the provided rewrite options.

The default behavior is to just deduplicate the sourcemap, something that automatically takes place. This for instance can be used to slightly compress sourcemaps if certain data is not wanted.

```
use swc_sourcemap::{SourceMap, RewriteOptions};
let sm = SourceMap::from_slice(input).unwrap();
let new_sm = sm.rewrite(&RewriteOptions {
    with_names: false,
    ..Default::default()
});
```
#### pub fn [adjust_mappings](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.adjust_mappings)(&mut self, adjustment: &[SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html))

#### pub fn [adjust_mappings](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.adjust_mappings)(&mut self, adjustment: &[SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html))

Adjusts the mappings in `self` using the mappings in `adjustment`.

Here is the intended use case for this function:

- You have a source file (for example, minified JS) `foo.js`and a corresponding sourcemap`foo.js.map`.
- You modify `foo.js`in some way and generate a sourcemap`transform.js.map`representing this modification. This can be done using`magic-string`, for example.
- You want a sourcemap that is “like” `foo.js.map`, but takes the changes you made to`foo.js`into account.

Then `foo.js.map.adjust_mappings(transform.js.map)` is the desired sourcemap.

This function assumes that `adjustment` contains no relevant information except for mappings.
All information about sources and names is copied from `self`.

Note that the resulting sourcemap will be at most as fine-grained as `self.`.

# Struct SourceMapBuilder

`pub struct SourceMapBuilder { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`__base`## Expand description

Helper for sourcemap generation

This helper exists because generating and modifying `SourceMap`
objects is generally not very comfortable.  As a general aid this
type can help.

Given a location, name and minified source file resolve a minified name to an original function name.

This invokes some guesswork and requires access to the original minified source. This will not yield proper results for anonymous functions or functions that do not have clear function names. (For instance it’s recommended that dotted function names are not passed to this function).

#### pub fn [adjust_mappings](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.adjust_mappings)(&mut self, adjustment: &[SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html))

#### pub fn [adjust_mappings](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.adjust_mappings)(&mut self, adjustment: &[SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html))

Adjusts the mappings in `self` using the mappings in `adjustment`.

Here is the intended use case for this function:

- You have a source file (for example, minified JS) `foo.js`and a corresponding sourcemap`foo.js.map`.
- You modify `foo.js`in some way and generate a sourcemap`transform.js.map`representing this modification. This can be done using`magic-string`, for example.
- You want a sourcemap that is “like” `foo.js.map`, but takes the changes you made to`foo.js`into account.

Then `foo.js.map.adjust_mappings(transform.js.map)` is the desired sourcemap.

This function assumes that `adjustment` contains no relevant information except for mappings.
All information about sources and names is copied from `self`.

Note that the resulting sourcemap will be at most as fine-grained as `self.`.

    x_facebook_offsets: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)>>>,
    x_metro_module_paths: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>>,
) -> [SourceMapIndex](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMapIndex.html)

Constructs a new sourcemap index from raw components including the facebook RAM bundle extensions.

- `file`: an optional filename of the index
- `sections`: a vector of source map index sections
- `x_facebook_offsets`: a vector of facebook offsets
- `x_metro_module_paths`: a vector of metro module paths

#### pub fn [get_original_function_name](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_original_function_name)(

#### pub fn [get_original_function_name](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_original_function_name)(
    &self,
    line: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
    col: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html),
    minified_name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    sv: &[SourceView](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceView.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&BytesStr>

Given a location, name and minified source file resolve a minified name to an original function name.

This invokes some guesswork and requires access to the original minified source. This will not yield proper results for anonymous functions or functions that do not have clear function names. (For instance it’s recommended that dotted function names are not passed to this function).

#### pub fn [lookup_token](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.lookup_token)(&self, line: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html), col: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Token](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Token.html)<'_>>

#### pub fn [lookup_token](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.lookup_token)(&self, line: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html), col: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Token](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Token.html)<'_>>

Looks up the closest token to a given line and column.

This requires that the referenced sourcemaps are actually loaded. If a sourcemap is encountered that is not embedded but just externally referenced it is silently skipped.

Flattens an indexed sourcemap into a regular one. This requires that all referenced sourcemaps are attached.

#### pub fn [flatten_and_rewrite](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.flatten_and_rewrite)(
    self,
    options: &[RewriteOptions](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.RewriteOptions.html)<'_>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html), [Error](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Error.html)>

#### pub fn [flatten_and_rewrite](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.flatten_and_rewrite)(
    self,
    options: &[RewriteOptions](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.RewriteOptions.html)<'_>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html), [Error](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Error.html)>

Flattens an indexed sourcemap into a regular one and automatically rewrites it. This is more useful than plain flattening as this will cause the sourcemap to be properly deduplicated.

#### pub fn [adjust_sections_offset_rows](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.adjust_sections_offset_rows)(&mut self, amount: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

#### pub fn [adjust_sections_offset_rows](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.adjust_sections_offset_rows)(&mut self, amount: [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Adjusts all of the sections’ offset rows by the given amount. Returns a boolean indicating whether the adjustment was successful (false indicating that not all of the sections could be adjusted because we overflowed the u32, true if adjustment was successful). If false is returned, then the sourcemap index is unchanged.

Remove duplicates from sections of consecutive identical elements, while keeping a count of
how many repeated elements were present.
This will determine equality using a comparison function.
If the iterator is sorted, all elements will be unique.

[Read more]If there are elements and they are all equal, return a single copy of that element.
If there are no elements, return an Error containing None.
If there are elements and they are not all equal, return a tuple containing the first
two non-equal elements found.

# Struct SourceView

`pub struct SourceView { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`__base`## Expand description

Provides efficient access to minified sources.

This type is used to implement fairly efficient source mapping operations.

## Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#implementations)

#### pub fn [get_original_function_name](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_original_function_name)<'map>(
    &self,
    token: [Token](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Token.html)<'map>,
    minified_name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&'map BytesStr>

#### pub fn [get_original_function_name](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_original_function_name)<'map>(
    &self,
    token: [Token](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Token.html)<'map>,
    minified_name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&'map BytesStr>

Given a token and minified function name this attemps to resolve the name to an original function name.

This invokes some guesswork and requires access to the original minified source. This will not yield proper results for anonymous functions or functions that do not have clear function names. (For instance it’s recommended that dotted function names are not passed to this function).

`iter_partition_in_place`)Reorders the elements of this iterator

Remove duplicates from sections of consecutive identical elements, while keeping a count of
how many repeated elements were present.
This will determine equality using a comparison function.
If the iterator is sorted, all elements will be unique.

[Read more]If there are elements and they are all equal, return a single copy of that element.
If there are no elements, return an Error containing None.
If there are elements and they are not all equal, return a tuple containing the first
two non-equal elements found.

# BytePos in swc_core::common - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_core/common/struct.BytePos.html

# Struct BytePos

`#[repr(C)]pub struct BytePos(pub `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html));**crate feature**only.

`__common`## Expand description

A byte offset. Keep this small (currently 32-bits), as AST contains a lot of them.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#reserved)Reserved

-
0 is reserved for dummy spans. It means `BytePos(0)`means the`BytePos`is synthesized by the compiler.
-
Values larger than `u32::MAX - 2^16`are reserved for the comments.

`u32::MAX` is special value used to generate source map entries.

## Tuple Fields[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#fields)

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#structfield.0)

`0: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)## Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#implementations)

Dummy position. This is reserved for synthesized spans.

#### pub const [PLACEHOLDER](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#associatedconstant.PLACEHOLDER): [BytePos](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.BytePos.html)

**crate features **`__ecma` and `__utils` only.

#### pub const [PLACEHOLDER](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#associatedconstant.PLACEHOLDER): [BytePos](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.BytePos.html)

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `__utils`Placeholders, commonly used where names are required, but the names are not referenced elsewhere.

Reserved for PURE comments. e.g. `/* #__PURE__ */`

# Struct CharPos

`#[repr(C)]pub struct CharPos(pub `[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html));Available on

**crate feature**only.`__common`## Expand description

A character offset. Because of multibyte utf8 characters, a byte offset is not equivalent to a character offset. The SourceMap will convert BytePos values to CharPos values as necessary.

# Loc in swc_core::common - Rust

# Struct Loc

```
pub struct Loc {
    pub file:
```
[Arc](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/sync/struct.Lrc.html)<[SourceFile](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceFile.html)>,
    pub line: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
    pub col: [CharPos](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.CharPos.html),
    pub col_display: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html),
}**crate feature**only.

`__common`## Expand description

A source code location used for error reporting.

Note: This struct intentionally does not implement rkyv’s archieve to avoid redundant data copy (https://github.com/swc-project/swc/issues/5471) source_map_proxy constructs plugin-side Loc instead with shared SourceFile instance.

# MultiSpan in swc_core::common - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_core/common/struct.MultiSpan.html

# Struct MultiSpan

`#[repr(C)]pub struct MultiSpan { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`__common`## Expand description

A collection of spans. Spans have two orthogonal attributes:

- they can be *primary spans*. In this case they are the locus of the error, and would be rendered with`^^^`.
- they can have a *label*. In this case, the label is written next to the mark in the snippet when we render.

## Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#implementations)

# SourceMap in swc_core::common - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_core/common/struct.SourceMap.html

# Struct SourceMap

`pub struct SourceMap { /* private fields */ }`**crate feature**only.

`__common`## Expand description

The interner for spans.

As most spans are simply stored, we store them as interned form.

- Each ast node only stores pointer to actual data ([BytePos](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.BytePos.html)).
- The pointers ([BytePos](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.BytePos.html)) can be converted to file name, line and column using this struct.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#note)Note

This struct should be shared. `swc_common` uses [crate::sync::Lrc](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/sync/struct.Lrc.html), which is
[std::rc::Rc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/rc/struct.Rc.html) or [std::sync::Arc](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/sync/struct.Lrc.html), depending on the compile option, for this
purpose.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#note-for-bundler-authors)Note for bundler authors

If you are bundling modules, you should share this struct while parsing
modules. Otherwise, you have to implement a code generator which accepts
multiple [SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html).

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `__utils`Returns `Some(span)`, a union of the lhs and rhs span.  The lhs must
precede the rhs. If there are gaps between lhs and rhs, the
resulting union will cross these gaps. For this to work, the spans
have to be:

- the ctxt of both spans much match
- the lhs span needs to end on the same line the rhs span begins
- the lhs span must start at or before the rhs span

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `__utils`Take the span of a type parameter in a function signature and try to generate a span for the function name (with generics) and a new snippet for this span with the pointed type parameter as a new local type parameter.

For instance:

[ⓘ](https://rustdoc.swc.rs)

```
// Given span
fn my_function(param: T)
//                    ^ Original span
// Result
fn my_function(param: T)
// ^^^^^^^^^^^ Generated span with snippet `my_function<T>`
```
Attention: The method used is very fragile since it essentially duplicates the work of the parser. If you need to use this function or something similar, please consider updating the source_map functions and this function to something more robust.

# Span in swc_core::common - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_core/common/struct.Span.html

# Struct Span

**crate feature**only.

`__common`## Expand description

Spans represent a region of code, used for error reporting.

Positions in
spans are *absolute* positions from the beginning of the `source_map`, not
positions relative to `SourceFile`s. Methods on the `SourceMap` can be used
to relate spans back to the original source.
You must be careful if the span crosses more than one file - you will not be
able to use many of the functions on spans in `source_map` and you cannot
assume that the length of the `span = hi - lo`; there may be space in the
`BytePos` range between files.

# CacheCell in swc_core::common::cache - Rust

Source: https://rustdoc.swc.rs/swc_core/common/cache/struct.CacheCell.html

# Struct CacheCell

`pub struct CacheCell<T>(/* private fields */);`**crate feature**only.

`__common`## Implementations[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#implementations)

Gets the reference to the underlying value.

Returns `None` if the cell is empty, or being initialized. This
method never blocks.

Gets the reference to the underlying value, blocking the current thread until it is set.

```
use once_cell::sync::OnceCell;
let mut cell = std::sync::Arc::new(OnceCell::new());
let t = std::thread::spawn({
    let cell = std::sync::Arc::clone(&cell);
    move || cell.set(92).unwrap()
});
// Returns immediately, but might return None.
let _value_or_none = cell.get();
// Will return 92, but might block until the other thread does `.set`.
let value: &u32 = cell.wait();
assert_eq!(*value, 92);
t.join().unwrap();
```
#### pub unsafe fn [get_unchecked](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_unchecked)(&self) -> [&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

**crate features **`__ecma` and `ecma_ast` only.

#### pub unsafe fn [get_unchecked](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_unchecked)(&self) -> [&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `ecma_ast`Get the reference to the underlying value, without checking if the cell is initialized.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#safety)Safety

Caller must ensure that the cell is in initialized state, and that the contents are acquired by (synchronized to) this thread.

Sets the contents of this cell to `value`.

Returns `Ok(())` if the cell was empty and `Err(value)` if it was
full.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example)Example

```
use once_cell::sync::OnceCell;
static CELL: OnceCell<i32> = OnceCell::new();
fn main() {
    assert!(CELL.get().is_none());
    std::thread::spawn(|| {
        assert_eq!(CELL.set(92), Ok(()));
    }).join().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(CELL.set(62), Err(62));
    assert_eq!(CELL.get(), Some(&92));
}
```
#### pub fn [try_insert](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.try_insert)(&self, value: T) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html), ([&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html), T)>

**crate features **`__ecma` and `ecma_ast` only.

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `ecma_ast`#### pub fn [get_or_init](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_or_init)<F>(&self, f: F) -> [&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

**crate features **`__ecma` and `ecma_ast` only.

#### pub fn [get_or_init](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_or_init)<F>(&self, f: F) -> [&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `ecma_ast`Gets the contents of the cell, initializing it with `f` if the cell
was empty.

Many threads may call `get_or_init` concurrently with different
initializing functions, but it is guaranteed that only one function
will be executed.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics)Panics

If `f` panics, the panic is propagated to the caller, and the cell
remains uninitialized.

It is an error to reentrantly initialize the cell from `f`. The
exact outcome is unspecified. Current implementation deadlocks, but
this may be changed to a panic in the future.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example-2)Example

```
use once_cell::sync::OnceCell;
let cell = OnceCell::new();
let value = cell.get_or_init(|| 92);
assert_eq!(value, &92);
let value = cell.get_or_init(|| unreachable!());
assert_eq!(value, &92);
```
#### pub fn [get_or_try_init](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_or_try_init)<F, E>(&self, f: F) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html), E>

**crate features **`__ecma` and `ecma_ast` only.

#### pub fn [get_or_try_init](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_or_try_init)<F, E>(&self, f: F) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[&T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html), E>

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `ecma_ast`Gets the contents of the cell, initializing it with `f` if
the cell was empty. If the cell was empty and `f` failed, an
error is returned.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics-1)Panics

If `f` panics, the panic is propagated to the caller, and
the cell remains uninitialized.

It is an error to reentrantly initialize the cell from `f`.
The exact outcome is unspecified. Current implementation
deadlocks, but this may be changed to a panic in the future.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example-3)Example

```
use once_cell::sync::OnceCell;
let cell = OnceCell::new();
assert_eq!(cell.get_or_try_init(|| Err(())), Err(()));
assert!(cell.get().is_none());
let value = cell.get_or_try_init(|| -> Result<i32, ()> {
    Ok(92)
});
assert_eq!(value, Ok(&92));
assert_eq!(cell.get(), Some(&92))
```

# Struct CodeSuggestion

```
#[repr(C)]pub struct CodeSuggestion {
    pub substitutions:
```
[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Substitution](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Substitution.html)>,
    pub msg: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub show_code_when_inline: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub applicability: [Applicability](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Applicability.html),
}**crate feature**only.

`__common`## Fields[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#fields)

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#structfield.substitutions)

`substitutions: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Substitution](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Substitution.html)>Each substitute can have multiple variants due to multiple applicable suggestions

`foo.bar` might be replaced with `a.b` or `x.y` by replacing
`foo` and `bar` on their own:

[ⓘ](https://rustdoc.swc.rs)

```
vec![
    Substitution {
        parts: vec![(0..3, "a"), (4..7, "b")],
    },
    Substitution {
        parts: vec![(0..3, "x"), (4..7, "y")],
    },
]
```
or by replacing the entire span:

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#structfield.msg)

`msg: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#structfield.show_code_when_inline)

`show_code_when_inline: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#structfield.applicability)

`applicability: `[Applicability](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Applicability.html)Whether or not the suggestion is approximate

Sometimes we may show suggestions with placeholders, which are useful for users but not useful for tools like rustfix

`__common`## Expand description

Represents a diagnostic message with its level, message, unique identifier, span, children, and suggestions.

## Fields[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#fields)

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#structfield.level)

`level: `[Level](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.Level.html)The level of the diagnostic (e.g., error, warning, help)

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#structfield.message)

`message: `[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[Message](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.Message.html)>The message(s) associated with the diagnostic

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#structfield.code)

`code: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[DiagnosticId](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/enum.DiagnosticId.html)>A unique identifier for the diagnostic, which can be used to look up more information

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#structfield.span)

`span: `[MultiSpan](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.MultiSpan.html)The span of the source code where the diagnostic is located

`span_suggestion_with_applicability`**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `__utils`Prints out a message with a suggested edit of the code.

In case of short messages and a simple suggestion, rustc displays it as a label like

“try adding parentheses: `(tup.0).1`”

The message

- should not end in any punctuation (a `:`is added automatically)
- should not be a question
- should not contain any parts like “the following”, “as shown”
- may look like “to do xyz, use” or “to do xyz, use abc”
- may contain a name of a function, variable or type, but not whole expressions

See `CodeSuggestion` for more information.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.to_pretty_string)#### fn [to_pretty_string]<'a>(
    &self,
    cm: &'a [SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html),
    skip_filename: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    handler: &'a GraphicalReportHandler,
) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.to_pretty_string)

#### fn [to_pretty_string]<'a>(
    &self,
    cm: &'a [SourceMap](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/struct.SourceMap.html),
    skip_filename: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    handler: &'a GraphicalReportHandler,
) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

Converts the diagnostic into a pretty-printed string, suitable for display.

This method is used to generate a human-readable string representation
of the diagnostic. It utilizes the `PrettyDiagnostic` struct to
format the diagnostic information.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#parameters)Parameters

- `cm`: A reference to the- `SourceMap`used for mapping source code locations.
- `skip_filename`: A boolean indicating whether to skip including filenames in the output.
- `handler`: A reference to the- `GraphicalReportHandler`used for handling graphical reports.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#returns)Returns

A `String` containing the pretty-printed diagnostic information.

`__common`## Expand description

Used for emitting structured error messages and other diagnostic information.

If there is some state in a downstream crate you would like to
access in the methods of `DiagnosticBuilder` here, consider
extending `HandlerFlags`, accessed via `self.handler.flags`.

#### pub fn [delay_as_bug](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.delay_as_bug)(&mut self)

**crate features **`__ecma` and `__utils` only.

#### pub fn [delay_as_bug](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.delay_as_bug)(&mut self)

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `__utils`Delay emission of this diagnostic as a bug.

This can be useful in contexts where an error indicates a bug but typically this only happens when other compilation errors have already happened. In those cases this can be used to defer emission of this diagnostic as a bug in the compiler only if no other errors have been emitted.

In the meantime, though, callsites are required to deal with the “bug” locally in whichever way makes the most sense.

`span_suggestion_with_applicability`**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `__utils`Prints out a message with a suggested edit of the code.

In case of short messages and a simple suggestion, rustc displays it as a label like

“try adding parentheses: `(tup.0).1`”

The message

- should not end in any punctuation (a `:`is added automatically)
- should not be a question
- should not contain any parts like “the following”, “as shown”
- may look like “to do xyz, use” or “to do xyz, use abc”
- may contain a name of a function, variable or type, but not whole expressions

See `CodeSuggestion` for more information.

    /* private fields */
}**crate feature**only.

`__common`## Expand description

A handler deals with errors; certain errors (fatal, bug, unimpl) may cause immediate exit, others log errors for later reporting.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#example)Example

`swc` provides a global-like variable ([HANDLER](https://rustdoc.swc.rs/plugin/errors/static.HANDLER.html)) of type `Handler` that can
be used to report errors.

You can refer to [the lint rules](https://github.com/swc-project/swc/tree/main/crates/swc_ecma_lints/src/rules) for other example usages.
All lint rules have code for error reporting.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#error-reporting-in-swc)Error reporting in swc

[ⓘ](https://rustdoc.swc.rs)

```
use swc_common::errors::HANDLER;
    HANDLER.with(|handler| {
        // You can access the handler for the current file using HANDLER.with.
        // We now report an error
        // `struct_span_err` creates a builder for a diagnostic.
        // The span passed to `struct_span_err` will used to point the problematic code.
        //
        // You may provide additional information, like a previous declaration of parameter.
        handler
            .struct_span_err(
                span,
                &format!("`{}` used as parameter more than once", atom),
            )
            .span_note(
                old_span,
                &format!("previous definition of `{}` here", atom),
            )
            .emit();
    });
```

`__ecma` and `__utils`Resets the diagnostic error count as well as the cached emitted diagnostics.

NOTE: DO NOT call this function from rustc. It is only meant to be
called from external tools that want to reuse a `Parser` cleaning
the previously emitted diagnostics as well as the overall count of
emitted error diagnostics.

Remove duplicates from sections of consecutive identical elements, while keeping a count of
how many repeated elements were present.
This will determine equality using a comparison function.
If the iterator is sorted, all elements will be unique.

[Read more]If there are elements and they are all equal, return a single copy of that element.
If there are no elements, return an Error containing None.
If there are elements and they are not all equal, return a tuple containing the first
two non-equal elements found.

# All in swc_core::common::pass - Rust

# Struct All

```
pub struct All<V> {
    pub visitor: V,
}
```
Available on

**crate feature**only.`__common`## Expand description

Visit all children nodes. This converts `VisitAll` to `Visit`. The type
parameter `V` should implement `VisitAll` and `All<V>` implements `Visit`.

**crate features**only.

`__ecma` and `__utils`Returns the total number of elements the vector can hold without reallocating.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples)Examples

```
let mut vec: Vec<i32> = Vec::with_capacity(10);
vec.push(42);
assert!(vec.capacity() >= 10);
```
A vector with zero-sized elements will always have a capacity of usize::MAX:

```
#[derive(Clone)]
struct ZeroSized;
fn main() {
    assert_eq!(std::mem::size_of::<ZeroSized>(), 0);
    let v = vec![ZeroSized; 0];
    assert_eq!(v.capacity(), usize::MAX);
}
```
Returns a raw pointer to the vector’s buffer, or a dangling raw pointer valid for zero sized reads if the vector didn’t allocate.

The caller must ensure that the vector outlives the pointer this function returns, or else it will end up dangling. Modifying the vector may cause its buffer to be reallocated, which would also make any pointers to it invalid.

The caller must also ensure that the memory the pointer (non-transitively) points to
is never written to (except inside an `UnsafeCell`) using this pointer or any pointer
derived from it. If you need to mutate the contents of the slice, use [ as_mut_ptr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.as_mut_ptr).

This method guarantees that for the purpose of the aliasing model, this method
does not materialize a reference to the underlying slice, and thus the returned pointer
will remain valid when mixed with other calls to [ as_ptr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.as_ptr),

[, and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.as_mut_ptr)

`as_mut_ptr`[. Note that calling other methods that materialize mutable references to the slice, or mutable references to specific elements you are planning on accessing through this pointer, as well as writing to those elements, may still invalidate this pointer. See the second example below for how this guarantee can be used.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html#method.as_non_null)

`as_non_null`[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
let x = vec![1, 2, 4];
let x_ptr = x.as_ptr();
unsafe {
    for i in 0..x.len() {
        assert_eq!(*x_ptr.add(i), 1 << i);
    }
}
```
Due to the aliasing guarantee, the following code is legal:

```
unsafe {
    let mut v = vec![0, 1, 2];
    let ptr1 = v.as_ptr();
    let _ = ptr1.read();
    let ptr2 = v.as_mut_ptr().offset(2);
    ptr2.write(2);
    // Notably, the write to `ptr2` did *not* invalidate `ptr1`
    // because it mutated a different element:
    let _ = ptr1.read();
}
```
Returns a reference to the underlying allocator.

Returns a mutable reference to the first element of the slice, or `None` if it is empty.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
let x = &mut [0, 1, 2];
if let Some(first) = x.first_mut() {
    *first = 5;
}
assert_eq!(x, &[5, 1, 2]);
let y: &mut [i32] = &mut [];
assert_eq!(None, y.first_mut());
```

or `None`if out of bounds.

#### pub unsafe fn [get_unchecked](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.get_unchecked)<I>(
    &self,
    index: I,
) -> &<I as [SliceIndex](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/index/trait.SliceIndex.html)<[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html)>>::[Output](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/slice/index/trait.SliceIndex.html#associatedtype.Output)

Returns a reference to an element or subslice, without doing bounds checking.

For a safe alternative see [ get](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.get).

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#safety)Safety

Calling this method with an out-of-bounds index is * undefined behavior*
even if the resulting reference is not used.

You can think of this like `.get(index).unwrap_unchecked()`.  It’s UB
to call `.get_unchecked(len)`, even if you immediately convert to a
pointer.  And it’s UB to call `.get_unchecked(..len + 1)`,
`.get_unchecked(..=len)`, or similar.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-25)Examples

```
let x = &[1, 2, 4];
unsafe {
    assert_eq!(x.get_unchecked(1), &2);
}
```

    let elem = x.get_unchecked_mut(1);
    *elem = 13;
}
assert_eq!(x, &[1, 13, 4]);
```
Returns a raw pointer to the slice’s buffer.

The caller must ensure that the slice outlives the pointer this function returns, or else it will end up dangling.

The caller must also ensure that the memory the pointer (non-transitively) points to
is never written to (except inside an `UnsafeCell`) using this pointer or any pointer
derived from it. If you need to mutate the contents of the slice, use [ as_mut_ptr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_mut_ptr).

Modifying the container referenced by this slice may cause its buffer to be reallocated, which would also make any pointers to it invalid.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-27)Examples

```
let x = &[1, 2, 4];
let x_ptr = x.as_ptr();
unsafe {
    for i in 0..x.len() {
        assert_eq!(x.get_unchecked(i), &*x_ptr.add(i));
    }
}
```

1.48.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#786)#### pub fn [as_ptr_range](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.as_ptr_range)(&self) -> [Range](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/range/struct.Range.html)<[*const T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)>

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#786)

#### pub fn [as_ptr_range](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.as_ptr_range)(&self) -> [Range](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/range/struct.Range.html)<[*const T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.pointer.html)>

Returns the two raw pointers spanning the slice.

The returned range is half-open, which means that the end pointer
points *one past* the last element of the slice. This way, an empty
slice is represented by two equal pointers, and the difference between
the two pointers represents the size of the slice.

See [ as_ptr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_ptr) for warnings on using these pointers. The end pointer
requires extra caution, as it does not point to a valid element in the
slice.

This function is useful for interacting with foreign interfaces which use two pointers to refer to a range of elements in memory, as is common in C++.

It can also be useful to check if a pointer to an element refers to an element of this slice:

```
let a = [1, 2, 3];
let x = &a[1] as *const _;
let y = &5 as *const _;
assert!(a.as_ptr_range().contains(&x));
assert!(!a.as_ptr_range().contains(&y));
```

Calling this method with an out-of-bounds index is * undefined behavior*.

Returns an iterator over all contiguous windows of length
`size`. The windows overlap. If the slice is shorter than
`size`, the iterator returns no values.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics-1)Panics

Panics if `size` is zero.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-34)Examples

```
let slice = ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm'];
let mut iter = slice.windows(3);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['l', 'o', 'r']);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['o', 'r', 'e']);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &['r', 'e', 'm']);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
If the slice is shorter than `size`:

```
let slice = ['f', 'o', 'o'];
let mut iter = slice.windows(4);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
Because the [Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html) trait cannot represent the required lifetimes,
there is no `windows_mut` analog to `windows`;
`[0,1,2].windows_mut(2).collect()` would violate [the rules of references](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch04-02-references-and-borrowing.html#the-rules-of-references)
(though a [LendingIterator](https://blog.rust-lang.org/2022/10/28/gats-stabilization.html) analog is possible). You can sometimes use
[ Cell::as_slice_of_cells](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cell/struct.Cell.html#method.as_slice_of_cells) in
conjunction with

`windows` instead:```
use std::cell::Cell;
let mut array = ['R', 'u', 's', 't', ' ', '2', '0', '1', '5'];
let slice = &mut array[..];
let slice_of_cells: &[Cell<char>] = Cell::from_mut(slice).as_slice_of_cells();
for w in slice_of_cells.windows(3) {
    Cell::swap(&w[0], &w[2]);
}
assert_eq!(array, ['s', 't', ' ', '2', '0', '1', '5', 'u', 'R']);
```

beginning of the slice.

The chunks are slices and do not overlap. If `chunk_size` does not divide the length of the
slice, then the last chunk will not have length `chunk_size`.

See [ chunks_exact](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.chunks_exact) for a variant of this iterator that returns chunks of always exactly

`chunk_size` elements, and [for the same iterator but starting at the end of the slice.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.rchunks)

`rchunks`[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics-2)Panics

1.88.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1310)#### pub unsafe fn [as_chunks_unchecked](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.as_chunks_unchecked)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&self) -> &[[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)]

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1310)

#### pub unsafe fn [as_chunks_unchecked](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.as_chunks_unchecked)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&self) -> &[[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)]

Splits the slice into a slice of `N`-element arrays,
assuming that there’s no remainder.

This is the inverse operation to [ as_flattened](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_flattened).

As this is `unsafe`, consider whether you could use [ as_chunks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_chunks) or

[instead, perhaps via something like](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_rchunks)

`as_rchunks``if let (chunks, []) = slice.as_chunks()` or
`let (chunks, []) = slice.as_chunks() else { unreachable!() };`.[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#safety-3)Safety

This may only be called when

- The slice splits exactly into `N`-element chunks (aka`self.len() % N == 0`).
- `N != 0`.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-39)Examples

```
let slice: &[char] = &['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm', '!'];
let chunks: &[[char; 1]] =
    // SAFETY: 1-element chunks never have remainder
    unsafe { slice.as_chunks_unchecked() };
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['l'], ['o'], ['r'], ['e'], ['m'], ['!']]);
let chunks: &[[char; 3]] =
    // SAFETY: The slice length (6) is a multiple of 3
    unsafe { slice.as_chunks_unchecked() };
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['l', 'o', 'r'], ['e', 'm', '!']]);
// These would be unsound:
// let chunks: &[[_; 5]] = slice.as_chunks_unchecked() // The slice length is not a multiple of 5
// let chunks: &[[_; 0]] = slice.as_chunks_unchecked() // Zero-length chunks are never allowed
```
Splits the slice into a slice of `N`-element arrays,
starting at the beginning of the slice,
and a remainder slice with length strictly less than `N`.

The remainder is meaningful in the division sense.  Given
`let (chunks, remainder) = slice.as_chunks()`, then:

- `chunks.len()`equals- `slice.len() / N`,
- `remainder.len()`equals- `slice.len() % N`, and
- `slice.len()`equals- `chunks.len() * N + remainder.len()`.

You can flatten the chunks back into a slice-of-`T` with [ as_flattened](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_flattened).

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics-6)Panics

Panics if `N` is zero.

Note that this check is against a const generic parameter, not a runtime value, and thus a particular monomorphization will either always panic or it will never panic.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-40)Examples

```
let slice = ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm'];
let (chunks, remainder) = slice.as_chunks();
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['l', 'o'], ['r', 'e']]);
assert_eq!(remainder, &['m']);
```
If you expect the slice to be an exact multiple, you can combine
`let`-`else` with an empty slice pattern:

```
let slice = ['R', 'u', 's', 't'];
let (chunks, []) = slice.as_chunks::<2>() else {
    panic!("slice didn't have even length")
};
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['R', 'u'], ['s', 't']]);
```
1.88.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1415)#### pub fn [as_rchunks](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.as_rchunks)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&self) -> (&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)])

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1415)

#### pub fn [as_rchunks](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.as_rchunks)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&self) -> (&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)])

Splits the slice into a slice of `N`-element arrays,
starting at the end of the slice,
and a remainder slice with length strictly less than `N`.

The remainder is meaningful in the division sense.  Given
`let (remainder, chunks) = slice.as_rchunks()`, then:

- `remainder.len()`equals- `slice.len() % N`,
- `chunks.len()`equals- `slice.len() / N`, and
- `slice.len()`equals- `chunks.len() * N + remainder.len()`.

You can flatten the chunks back into a slice-of-`T` with [ as_flattened](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_flattened).

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics-7)Panics

Panics if `N` is zero.

Note that this check is against a const generic parameter, not a runtime value, and thus a particular monomorphization will either always panic or it will never panic.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-41)Examples

```
let slice = ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm'];
let (remainder, chunks) = slice.as_rchunks();
assert_eq!(remainder, &['l']);

1.88.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1505)#### pub unsafe fn [as_chunks_unchecked_mut](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.as_chunks_unchecked_mut)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(
    &mut self,

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1505)

#### pub unsafe fn [as_chunks_unchecked_mut](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.as_chunks_unchecked_mut)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(
    &mut self,
) -> &mut [[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)]

Splits the slice into a slice of `N`-element arrays,
assuming that there’s no remainder.

This is the inverse operation to [ as_flattened_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_flattened_mut).

As this is `unsafe`, consider whether you could use [ as_chunks_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_chunks_mut) or

[instead, perhaps via something like](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_rchunks_mut)

`as_rchunks_mut``if let (chunks, []) = slice.as_chunks_mut()` or
`let (chunks, []) = slice.as_chunks_mut() else { unreachable!() };`.[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#safety-4)Safety

This may only be called when

- The slice splits exactly into `N`-element chunks (aka`self.len() % N == 0`).
- `N != 0`.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-43)Examples

```
let slice: &mut [char] = &mut ['l', 'o', 'r', 'e', 'm', '!'];
let chunks: &mut [[char; 1]] =
    // SAFETY: 1-element chunks never have remainder
    unsafe { slice.as_chunks_unchecked_mut() };
chunks[0] = ['L'];
assert_eq!(chunks, &[['L'], ['o'], ['r'], ['e'], ['m'], ['!']]);
let chunks: &mut [[char; 3]] =
    // SAFETY: The slice length (6) is a multiple of 3
    unsafe { slice.as_chunks_unchecked_mut() };
chunks[1] = ['a', 'x', '?'];
assert_eq!(slice, &['L', 'o', 'r', 'a', 'x', '?']);
// These would be unsound:
// let chunks: &[[_; 5]] = slice.as_chunks_unchecked_mut() // The slice length is not a multiple of 5
// let chunks: &[[_; 0]] = slice.as_chunks_unchecked_mut() // Zero-length chunks are never allowed
```
1.88.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1559)#### pub fn [as_chunks_mut](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.as_chunks_mut)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&mut self) -> (&mut [[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)], &mut [[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/slice/mod.rs.html#1559)

#### pub fn [as_chunks_mut](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.as_chunks_mut)<const N: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)>(&mut self) -> (&mut [[[T; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)], &mut [[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))

Splits the slice into a slice of `N`-element arrays,
starting at the beginning of the slice,
and a remainder slice with length strictly less than `N`.

The remainder is meaningful in the division sense.  Given
`let (chunks, remainder) = slice.as_chunks_mut()`, then:

- `chunks.len()`equals- `slice.len() / N`,
- `remainder.len()`equals- `slice.len() % N`, and
- `slice.len()`equals- `chunks.len() * N + remainder.len()`.

You can flatten the chunks back into a slice-of-`T` with [ as_flattened_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.as_flattened_mut).

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics-9)Panics

Panics if `N` is zero.

Note that this check is against a const generic parameter, not a runtime value, and thus a particular monomorphization will either always panic or it will never panic.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-44)Examples

```
let v = &mut [0, 0, 0, 0, 0];
let mut count = 1;
let (chunks, remainder) = v.as_chunks_mut();
remainder[0] = 9;
for chunk in chunks {
    *chunk = [count; 2];
    count += 1;
}
assert_eq!(v, &[1, 1, 2, 2, 9]);
```

Returns an iterator over the slice producing non-overlapping runs of elements using the predicate to separate them.

The predicate is called for every pair of consecutive elements,
meaning that it is called on `slice[0]` and `slice[1]`,
followed by `slice[1]` and `slice[2]`, and so on.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-52)Examples

```
let slice = &[1, 1, 1, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2];
let mut iter = slice.chunk_by(|a, b| a == b);
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[1, 1, 1][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[3, 3][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[2, 2, 2][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), None);
```
This method can be used to extract the sorted subslices:

```
let slice = &[1, 1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4];
let mut iter = slice.chunk_by(|a, b| a <= b);
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[1, 1, 2, 3][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[2, 3][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(&[2, 3, 4][..]));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), None);
```

Divides one slice into two at an index.

The first will contain all indices from `[0, mid)` (excluding
the index `mid` itself) and the second will contain all
indices from `[mid, len)` (excluding the index `len` itself).

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics-17)Panics

Panics if `mid > len`.  For a non-panicking alternative see
[ split_at_checked](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.split_at_checked).

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-54)Examples

```
let v = ['a', 'b', 'c'];
{
   let (left, right) = v.split_at(0);
   assert_eq!(left, []);
   assert_eq!(right, ['a', 'b', 'c']);
}
{
    let (left, right) = v.split_at(2);
    assert_eq!(left, ['a', 'b']);
    assert_eq!(right, ['c']);
}
{
    let (left, right) = v.split_at(3);
    assert_eq!(left, ['a', 'b', 'c']);
    assert_eq!(right, []);
}
```

Divides one mutable slice into two at an index.

The first will contain all indices from `[0, mid)` (excluding
the index `mid` itself) and the second will contain all
indices from `[mid, len)` (excluding the index `len` itself).

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#panics-18)Panics

Panics if `mid > len`.  For a non-panicking alternative see
[ split_at_mut_checked](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.split_at_mut_checked).

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-55)Examples

```
let mut v = [1, 0, 3, 0, 5, 6];
let (left, right) = v.split_at_mut(2);
assert_eq!(left, [1, 0]);
assert_eq!(right, [3, 0, 5, 6]);
left[1] = 2;
right[1] = 4;
assert_eq!(v, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
```

#### pub unsafe fn [split_at_unchecked](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#method.split_at_unchecked)(&self, mid: [usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html)) -> (&[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html), &[[T]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html))

Divides one slice into two at an index, without doing bounds checking.

The first will contain all indices from `[0, mid)` (excluding
the index `mid` itself) and the second will contain all
indices from `[mid, len)` (excluding the index `len` itself).

For a safe alternative see [ split_at](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.split_at).

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#safety-5)Safety

Calling this method with an out-of-bounds index is * undefined behavior*
even if the resulting reference is not used. The caller has to ensure that

`0 <= mid <= self.len()`.[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-56)Examples

```
let v = ['a', 'b', 'c'];
unsafe {
   let (left, right) = v.split_at_unchecked(0);
   assert_eq!(left, []);
   assert_eq!(right, ['a', 'b', 'c']);
}
unsafe {
    let (left, right) = v.split_at_unchecked(2);
    assert_eq!(left, ['a', 'b']);
    assert_eq!(right, ['c']);
}
unsafe {
    let (left, right) = v.split_at_unchecked(3);
    assert_eq!(left, ['a', 'b', 'c']);
    assert_eq!(right, []);
}
```

Divides one mutable slice into two at an index, without doing bounds checking.

The first will contain all indices from `[0, mid)` (excluding
the index `mid` itself) and the second will contain all
indices from `[mid, len)` (excluding the index `len` itself).

For a safe alternative see [ split_at_mut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.split_at_mut).

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#safety-6)Safety

Calling this method with an out-of-bounds index is * undefined behavior*
even if the resulting reference is not used. The caller has to ensure that

`0 <= mid <= self.len()`.[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-57)Examples

```
let mut v = [1, 0, 3, 0, 5, 6];
// scoped to restrict the lifetime of the borrows
unsafe {
    let (left, right) = v.split_at_mut_unchecked(2);
    assert_eq!(left, [1, 0]);
    assert_eq!(right, [3, 0, 5, 6]);
    left[1] = 2;
    right[1] = 4;
}
assert_eq!(v, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
```
Divides one slice into two at an index, returning `None` if the slice is
too short.

If `mid ≤ len` returns a pair of slices where the first will contain all
indices from `[0, mid)` (excluding the index `mid` itself) and the
second will contain all indices from `[mid, len)` (excluding the index
`len` itself).

Otherwise, if `mid > len`, returns `None`.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-58)Examples

```
let v = [1, -2, 3, -4, 5, -6];
{
   let (left, right) = v.split_at_checked(0).unwrap();
   assert_eq!(left, []);
   assert_eq!(right, [1, -2, 3, -4, 5, -6]);
}
{
    let (left, right) = v.split_at_checked(2).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(left, [1, -2]);
    assert_eq!(right, [3, -4, 5, -6]);
}
{
    let (left, right) = v.split_at_checked(6).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(left, [1, -2, 3, -4, 5, -6]);
    assert_eq!(right, []);
}
assert_eq!(None, v.split_at_checked(7));
```

Divides one mutable slice into two at an index, returning `None` if the
slice is too short.

If `mid ≤ len` returns a pair of slices where the first will contain all
indices from `[0, mid)` (excluding the index `mid` itself) and the
second will contain all indices from `[mid, len)` (excluding the index

Otherwise, if `mid > len`, returns `None`.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-59)Examples

```
let mut v = [1, 0, 3, 0, 5, 6];

    assert_eq!(left, [1, 0]);
    assert_eq!(right, [3, 0, 5, 6]);

    right[1] = 4;

assert_eq!(v, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]);
assert_eq!(None, v.split_at_mut_checked(7));
```
Returns an iterator over subslices separated by elements that match
`pred`. The matched element is not contained in the subslices.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-60)Examples

```
let slice = [10, 40, 33, 20];
let mut iter = slice.split(|num| num % 3 == 0);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[10, 40]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[20]);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
If the first element is matched, an empty slice will be the first item returned by the iterator. Similarly, if the last element in the slice is matched, an empty slice will be the last item returned by the iterator:

```
let slice = [10, 40, 33];
let mut iter = slice.split(|num| num % 3 == 0);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[10, 40]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[]);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
If two matched elements are directly adjacent, an empty slice will be present between them:

```
let slice = [10, 6, 33, 20];
let mut iter = slice.split(|num| num % 3 == 0);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[10]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[]);
assert_eq!(iter.next().unwrap(), &[20]);
assert!(iter.next().is_none());
```
Returns an iterator over mutable subslices separated by elements that
match `pred`. The matched element is not contained in the subslices.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-61)Examples

```
let mut v = [10, 40, 30, 20, 60, 50];
for group in v.split_mut(|num| *num % 3 == 0) {
    group[0] = 1;
}
assert_eq!(v, [1, 40, 30, 1, 60, 1]);
```

subslice as a terminator.

```

Returns an iterator over subslices separated by elements that match
`pred`, starting at the end of the slice and working backwards.
The matched element is not contained in the subslices.

[§](https://rustdoc.swc.rs#examples-64)Examples

```
let slice = [11, 22, 33, 0, 44, 55];

assert_eq!(iter.next(), None);
```
As with `split()`, if the first or last element is matched, an empty
slice will be the first (or last) item returned by the iterator.

```
